pin_row_note: headpin-column base row read on stack_349_351 (lowest visible base 555.7 at f349, ~556 at f350); ball centre 555 at f349 vs 557.5 at f348. The ball BOTTOM (y+r) reaches the headpin base row only at f354 (549.5 vs 550.1).
method: Every path point is a hand read from 3x gridded ball crops (gc_<f>.jpg) and lane-width crops with row brightness/|dx| profiles at the ball row (combo_/lane_<f>.jpg), plus tall 5x panels of each lane edge over rows ~515-610 for f342-357 (edge_L*/edge_R*.jpg), all on the SOURCE video decoded sequentially; board = 1 + 38*(x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x) with both edges read in the same frame at the ball centre row (board_contact repeats it at about y+r). Entry board is the median of edge-profile reads at pin_hit-1..+1, a pin-column ruler at four frames (headpin column = lowest base; 6 in column stagger = 5.49 units in this 38-unit convention) and a ball-diameter ruler (17 px = 7.8 units) at three frames.
limits: release+6 (f303) is inside the ball-invisible span 299-306, so the path starts at f307 (motion-blurred ball, r 29 from the blur extent). The left gutter runs into the image border at f321-335 (left_x 6-46), so those left edges are +-5 px; near the deck the left edge is a blurred diagonal and reads +-3-4 px, the right edge +-2-3 px, which is +-0.8-1.3 boards per path point at the far end (e.g. f352 reads 11.3 between 9.5 at f350 and 9.7 at f354). The pin rack is narrower than the edges: the 7 pin columns span 65 px against 92-95 px edge to edge (expected 36 in / 41.5 in = 0.87, seen 0.70), the same disagreement loop 1 found; pin ruler and edges still agree within ~1 board here because the ball is near the right edge. The task text's pin map (7-pin 33, 10-pin 7, 3 units per column) was NOT used: it disagrees with its own 7.8-unit ball scale; with it the pin reads would be about 2-3 boards higher. Ball radius at the deck is 8-9 px +-1, so the ball ruler is +-10-15 % in scale (f356 ball ruler 13.2 is the outlier). pin_row_frame uses the ball centre; at the far end the centre is ~r above the contact point, so the ball reaches the pin-base row with its contact point only at ~f354. Camera is handheld and pans ~3-5 px/frame at the end, so nothing is carried between frames.
